info.title: LawFive API
info.description: The API of a LawFive server, which the web app, the watch apps and the phone apps use. Generated from schema/src/endpoints.ts. https://lawfive.dev/llms.txt lists the same reference as smaller pages, with worked examples.

servers.description: A server of your own, or the demo

server.description: Its address, for example http://localhost:3000 for the demo.

tags.name: Server
tags.description: What the server is and offers.

tags.name: Accounts
tags.description: Signing up, in and out (Better Auth's endpoints). Browsers keep the session in a cookie and must send an Origin header matching the server's address; apps send no Origin, take the token from the set-auth-token response header and send it as Authorization: Bearer <token>.

tags.name: Linking a watch
tags.description: A watch links to an account with a code (RFC 8628): it asks for a code and shows it, someone signed in enters it on the web app's Link page and approves it, and the watch, polling meanwhile, gets its own token. That token only reaches the watch's endpoints (/v1/watch/), and of the account endpoints only sign-out and get-session (SEC-13); anything else answers 403.

tags.name: Records
tags.description: The user's records, one collection per kind. Ids are UUIDs made by the client, so a record created offline keeps its id. Every change raises version; an update sends the version it last saw and gets 409 if the record changed in the meantime. Deleted records are kept as markers so other devices learn of the deletion.

tags.name: Tracks
tags.description: GPS and heart rate for a match report (TRK-1 to TRK-3), in LawFive's own format whatever recorded them: convert from the source (RefSix, an activity file, a phone's health store) before uploading. Not part of sync, as tracks are big; fetch one when it's shown. The figures (distance, speeds, sprints, heart rate and zones) are worked out by the server each time.

tags.name: Sync
tags.description: Everything that changed since a device last looked.

tags.name: People
tags.description: Admins (USR-1) see everyone on the server, approve or decline new accounts (USR-4), make other admins, and make password reset links, suspend and delete accounts, and change who can sign up (USR-7); and make plans, named sets of limits, and put each account in one (PLAN-1 to PLAN-5). Everyone else gets 403.

tags.name: App sign-in
tags.description: Signing in on a phone with a code the web app shows, as a QR code or in letters (APP-13), instead of typing a password.

tags.name: Invitations
tags.description: Links that let someone make an account even when sign-up is closed (USR-3). Admins make and cancel them; the link opens the web app's invitation page, which looks the invitation up and signs up with it.

tags.name: Import
tags.description: Adding and updating matches from a spreadsheet, CSV or JSON file (IMP-1 to IMP-8). Apps read the file into rows; the server matches each row to a match (by LawFive id, else match number), finds or adds the venues, competitions and referees it names, and saves only what the row fills in. Check first with dryRun.

tags.name: Assignor calendars
tags.description: An assignor system's private calendar link (ArbiterSports, Assignr, HorizonWebRef, RefTown and others give each official one), which the server reads every 30 minutes into the account's matches through the import (FEED-1 to FEED-10): new games added, moved ones changed, ones gone before kickoff canceled. The link is a password, so it's kept encrypted and never sent back. Only a signed-in session can manage them.

tags.name: Calendar
tags.description: A private calendar feed of the user's matches (CAL-1 to CAL-5), for calendar apps to subscribe to.

tags.name: Stats
tags.description: Reports on the user's games (STAT-1 to STAT-4), worked out by the server so every app shows the same.

tags.name: Devices
tags.description: Where the account is signed in.

tags.name: Attachments
tags.description: Photos on matches, venues and referees (FILE-1 to FILE-5), kept by the server on its disk or in S3-compatible storage. Upload the file as multipart/form-data, ideally already made smaller (the web app sends at most 2000 pixels on the longest side, as a JPEG without its location and camera details) with a thumbnail; the server keeps what it's sent. The files are private: fetch them with the same sign-in. Deleting the record deletes its attachments. Only a signed-in session can use them for now.

tags.name: Export
tags.description: Everything in the account as one zip (DATA-2), and restoring one into an account (DATA-4), for backups and moving between servers. The zip has lawfive.json (what it is), README.md, records/<collection>.json (each an array of records as the API gives them), tracks/<match record id>.json, attachments.json and the photos in attachments/. Only a signed-in session can use them.

tags.name: Sharing
tags.description: A match's share link (DATA-7): an address nobody can guess that shows the match, its log and its track to anyone who has it, without signing in. Never the notes, fee, crew, contacts, player names or photos.

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description: URLs that hear about changes to the account's records (HOOK-1 to HOOK-5): matches, match reports, venues, referees, competitions and templates, however they were made (the web app, the API, a watch, an import). Each delivery is a signed JSON POST (WebhookPayload), retried up to five times over about three hours when it doesn't get a 2xx answer. Only a signed-in session can manage them.

tags.name: API keys
tags.description: Keys for scripts and integrations (KEY-1 to KEY-4), made in the web app's Settings. A key is sent like a session token, Authorization: Bearer <key>, and can use only the collections it was given (read, or read and write), plus the weather (with matches:read) and address search (with venues:write). Keys can't manage devices or other keys, and only a signed-in session can make or delete them.

tags.name: Watch
tags.description: What a Garmin watch uses, shaped for its little memory: matches in the form it starts one from, and finished matches as it saved them.

tags.name: Places
tags.description: Address search for placing venues on the map.

tags.name: Quiz
tags.description: The Laws of the Game quiz's questions (QUIZ-1).

tags.name: Weather
tags.description: Forecasts for the user's matches, and the weather finished matches were played in (WX-1 to WX-8). The server fetches and keeps forecasts; apps never call the weather service themselves.

post.description: Signs the new account in. With SIGN_UP=closed only an invitation can make one; with SIGN_UP=approval the account is pending until an admin approves it (USR-2 to USR-4). post.description:
Each row adds a match or updates one: the row's ID column (a LawFive match id) wins, else its match number (any source). Only the columns a row fills in change an existing match. Venues, pitches, competitions and referees are found by name, ignoring case (venues, pitches and referees by their other names too), and added when there's none (an API key then needs write access to those too). Rows with problems are skipped and the rest are saved; nothing is saved on a dry run.

The columns, by their headings (any case or spacing, so home_colour and homeColour work too, as do common other headings like Field for Pitch):

| Column | JSON | What it's for | Example | Needed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ID | `id` | LawFive's own ID for a match, as in a LawFive export. Leave it empty for a new match; with it, the row updates that match. | 5c1e2a9b-… | Optional |
| Match number | `matchNumber` | The league's or assignor's number for the match. Importing a file again with the same number updates the match instead of adding a copy. | BYL-1142 | Optional |
| Assignor | `assignor` | Who assigned you the match: a person, or the assigning group's name. | Dana Whitfield | Optional |
| Status | `status` | scheduled, played, abandoned, canceled or postponed. A new match is scheduled when it's empty. | scheduled | Optional |
| Date | `date` | The day of the match: 2026-11-07, or the way your computer writes dates (11/7/2026 in the US, 7/11/2026 in most other places). | 2026-11-07 | New matches* |
| Time | `time` | The kickoff time: 14:30 or 2:30 PM. A new match with a date needs one. | 2:30 PM | Optional |
| Kickoff | `kickoff` | The date and time together, instead of Date and Time. Add a UTC offset (2026-11-07T14:30-08:00) to fix the moment exactly. | 2026-11-07 14:30 | New matches* |
| Time zone | `timeZone` | Where the kickoff time is, by its name in the time zone database. Empty: the match's own time zone, or your computer's. | America/Los_Angeles | Optional |
| Home | `home` | The home team's name. | Strikers U12 | New matches* |
| Home short name | `homeShortName` | Up to 4 letters for the home team on the watch. Empty: made from both team names (the first three letters or digits of each, skipping the words both names start with), and it follows them when they change. | STR | Optional |
| Home color | `homeColour` | The home team's color on the watch: black, white, red, orange, yellow, green, blue or purple, or a hex code like #D71920. | red | Optional |
| Away | `away` | The away team's name. | Rovers U12 | New matches* |
| Away short name | `awayShortName` | Up to 4 letters for the away team on the watch. Empty: made from both team names (the first three letters or digits of each, skipping the words both names start with), and it follows them when they change. | ROV | Optional |
| Away color | `awayColour` | The away team's color on the watch, written like Home color. | #0057B8 | Optional |
| Competition | `competition` | The league, cup or tournament, by name. One you don't have yet is added, as a league. | Bay Youth League U12 Boys | Optional |
| Venue | `venue` | Where it's played, by name. One you don't have yet is added; give it an address and a place on the map in Venues. | Twin Creeks Sports Complex | Optional |
| Venue address | `venueAddress` | The venue's street address, for directions: given to a venue that's added, or one that has no address yet. | 969 Caribbean Dr, Sunnyvale, CA 94089 | Optional |
| Pitch | `pitch` | The pitch at the venue. It's added to the venue if the venue doesn't have it yet. | Field 3 | Optional |
| Match name | `matchName` | A name for the match itself, shown with the competition: a round, a final, a friendly's occasion. | Semi-final | Optional |
| Age group | `ageGroup` | As the league writes it: U12, U19, Adult, O35. | U12 | Optional |
| Gender | `gender` | Who plays: male, female or co-ed (boys, girls, men, women and mixed work too). | female | Optional |
| Role | `role` | Your role: referee, AR1, AR2 or fourth official. Empty: taken from a crew column with your name in it, if there is one. | AR1 | Optional |
| Referee | `referee` | The referee's name, or one of their other names. Your own name makes it your role; someone you haven't saved yet is added to Referees. TBD or empty: nobody yet. | Priya Natarajan | Optional |
| AR1 | `ar1` | The first assistant referee's name, written like Referee. | Sam Rivera | Optional |
| AR2 | `ar2` | The second assistant referee's name, written like Referee. | Jordan Lee | Optional |
| Fourth official | `fourthOfficial` | The fourth official's name, written like Referee. | Sam Rivera | Optional |
| Template | `template` | One of your match templates, by name, for its format (periods, their length, breaks). It must already exist. Empty for a new match: the competition's template, or 2 × 45 minutes. | U12 league: 2×30 | Optional |
| Periods | `periods` | How many periods, 1 to 4: 2 for halves, 4 for quarters, 1 for a tournament game of one period. Overrides the template's. | 2 | Optional |
| Period length (min) | `periodLength` | Minutes in each period. Overrides the template's. | 30 | Optional |
| Half-time (min) | `halfTime` | Minutes of break between periods. Overrides the template's. | 5 | Optional |
| Team size | `teamSize` | Players a side on the field, 1 to 11. Overrides the template's. | 9 | Optional |
| Fee | `fee` | What you're paid for the match, as a number. | 40.50 | Optional |
| Currency | `currency` | The fee's currency, as a three-letter code (USD, GBP, EUR). Empty: your currency in Settings. | USD | Optional |
| Paid | `paid` | Whether you've been paid the fee: yes or no. | no | Optional |
| Tags | `tags` | Labels to find and filter matches by, separated by commas. | league, needs AR | Optional |
| Notes | `notes` | Anything to remember for the match. | Bring the spare flags. | Optional |
| Outlook | `outlook` | What to expect: how competitive it'll be, the teams' strengths, history between them. | Top of the table meets second. | Optional |

\* A new match needs a date (Date and Time, or Kickoff) or its teams; everything else is optional, and an empty value never changes a match. API keys: need matches:write.

id.description: A pitch of one of the venues in from.

into.description: The pitch it's the same as: one of this venue's, or one kept from another. Its matches move to that pitch, its corners walked are added to it, and its name becomes another name of it.

name.description: Without into, the pitch is kept, under this name (its own, or a new one): no other pitch of the merged venue may have it.

pitches.description: What happens to each pitch of the venues in from: every one, once.

VenueMerge.description: Venues to merge into one (DUP-7): the venue's details, and what happens to each of the others' pitches.

venue.description: The venue they were merged into, as saved.

merged.description: How many venues were merged into it (and deleted).

matchesUpdated.description: Matches that now point at it, and at its pitches.

referee.description: The referee they were merged into, as saved.

merged.description: How many referees were merged into it (and deleted).

matchesUpdated.description: Matches whose crew now names it, including crew typed as one of its names.

MatchCount.description: How many matches a venue or referee has, or several as if merged.

reasons.description: Why it's likely the same as the one asked about ("Same address", "Same name, in a different order"), surest first; for the likeliest only.

DuplicateMember.description: A venue or referee as the duplicate finder and merge preview show it (DUP-2, DUP-7).

reasons.description: Why they're probably one, in a few words each.

members.description: Most matches first: the one a merge keeps unless the user picks another.

groups.description: Groups that are probably one venue or person, surest first.

of.description: How many venues or referees there are in all.

DuplicateGroups.description: Likely duplicates across all of the user's venues or referees (DUP-1, DUP-7).

likely.description: At most six, likeliest first, each with its reasons.

LikelyDuplicates.description: The venues or referees most likely the same as one (Merge with…, DUP-1, DUP-7).

others.description: Venues or referees that aren't the same as this one, nor as each other.

NotTheSame.description: Venues or referees the user says are different, so they aren't suggested together again (DUP-5).

from.description: The referees to merge into this one; they're deleted.

name.description: The name chosen so far; left out, or not one of theirs, the kept referee's.

email.description: The email chosen so far, where they differ.

phone.description: The phone number chosen so far, where they differ.

RefereeMergeDraft.description: A referee merge as chosen so far, to preview (DUP-4).

referees.description: The referee kept, then the others, in the order sent; each with its reasons when it's among the likeliest.

names.description: Every name to choose from: theirs and their other names, once each. The rest become other names.

name.description: The name that will be kept.

emails.description: Their emails, once each: a choice when there's more than one.

phones.description: Their phone numbers, once each: a choice when there's more than one.

together.description: Their matches as one referee, crew typed in under one of their names included; a match counts once.

merge.description: What to send to POST /v1/referees/{id}/merge to merge exactly this.

RefereeMergePreview.description: What merging these referees would make (DUP-4, DUP-11).

from.description: The venues to merge into this one; they're deleted.

name.description: The name chosen so far; left out, or not one of theirs, the kept venue's.

addressFrom.description: The venue whose address and parking were chosen so far, where they differ.

pitches.description: The pitches the user has chosen for so far; the rest get the suggestion. A name can be empty while it's being typed.

into.description: The pitch it's the same as.

name.description: Without into, kept, under this name.

VenueMergeDraft.description: A venue merge as chosen so far, to preview (DUP-7, DUP-8).

venues.description: The venue kept, then the others, in the order sent; each with its reasons when it's among the likeliest.

names.description: Every name to choose from: theirs and their other names, once each. The rest become other names.

name.description: The name that will be kept.

onMap.description: Whether its parking is on the map.

places.description: Their different addresses and parking spots, once each: a choice when there's more than one.

addressFrom.description: The venue whose address and parking will be kept.

name.description: Its name now.

venue.description: The venue it's from, when there are several.

corners.description: How many times its corners were walked on the watch (TRK-13).

check.description: Whether to look at it first (shown as Check); the rest are likely fine.

why.description: Why it's suggested as it is, in a few words.

into.description: The pitch it's the same as.

name.description: Without into, kept, under this name.

choice.description: What happens to it: the user's choice, else the suggestion.

targets.description: The pitches it can be the same as: those the merged venue keeps, under the names they'll have.

problem.description: What's wrong with its choice; the merge waits until there's none.

pitches.description: Every pitch of the venues merged away, riskiest first, then more matches and corners walked first (DUP-8). The order depends only on the venues, so rows stay put while the choices change.

notes.description: Things to know, such as corners walked over the 20 a pitch keeps.

problems.description: Pitches that need a look before merging.

merge.description: What to send to POST /v1/venues/{id}/merge to merge exactly this; none while there are problems.

VenueMergePreview.description: What merging these venues would make (DUP-7, DUP-8, DUP-11).

explanation.description: Why this option is right or wrong; shown after answering.

QuizRef.description: What a question is based on: a Law and section, or a protocol.

status.description: active, draft or retired; the API only sends active ones.

QuizBank.description: The Laws of the Game quiz's questions in one language.

bearer.description: Apps: the token from set-auth-token (signing in) or access_token (linking a watch).

session.name: better-auth.session_token
session.description: Browsers: the session cookie set by signing in.
